newsitem.title: USA: American Greetings to overhaul non-holiday cards.
newsitem.headline: American Greetings to overhaul non-holiday cards.

text.p: American Greetings Corp said Wednesday it plans to overhaul its non-holiday greeting card line, replacing 80 percent of cards offered over 16 months starting in July.
The company said costs of the overhaul are embedded in current projections and it does not expect the overhaul to affect earnings.
Under the change, 100 million new cards will be put in the market over those 16 months, the company said at a news conference at its corporate headquarters here.
The company said the new marketing strategy is based on changing lifestyle and demographic trends which are signaling new consumer communications needs.

"These emerging trends are changing consumer attitudes and will drive purchasing desisions going forward," president and chief operating officer Edward Fruchtenbaum said. "This is a magnitude of change in greeting cards seen only once each generation."
Changing demographics include changing attitudes about aging as people live longer, the company said.
Changing family dynamics, with more step parents and half siblings and more families with two people working, are also leading to the revamp, the company said.
For example, American Greetings will introduce smaller note-sized cards that can be slipped into a child's lunch box.
Also, in addition to the traditional "Get Well" cards, there will be cards that express words of encouragement to someone with a long-term illness.
Hallmark is number one in U.S. greeting card market share and American Greetings number two, American Greetings said.
The new strategy does not affect American Greetings' holiday cards, the company said.
The company is developing a marketing and advertising plan for the strategy, but did not release details about the campaign Wednesday.
The marketing plan will not be launched until the middle of 1998, when the roll out to the 30,000 retailers that carry American Greeting's products is underway.
American Greeting's shares were down 1/16 at 33-13/16.
Everyday and birthday card sales made up 44 percent of American Greetings' $2.16 billion sales in 1996, compared to 22 percent for holiday cards, the company said.
